brief.text:
No Week 1 games played yet — the season opens Wednesday (Seahawks-Patriots) and Thursday (49ers-Rams in Melbourne), with the rest of the league kicking off Sunday. Nothing to recap this Tuesday; the real recap starts next week.

GANGSTAS PARADISE (Sleeper) — lineup locked and healthy, every Q trending to clear by kickoff
Do now: nothing — lineup is set
Locks next 24h: none — first Sleeper-relevant kickoff is Herbert/Hampton Sunday 1:25 PM PT vs ARI; the overall week's first lock is Aubrey (DAL) Sunday, no Wed/Thu games on this roster
Lineup: no changes from the weekend plan. Higgins (heel) is limited in practice but Taylor says he and Ja'Marr will "be good by end of week"; Flowers (quad) got a positive Tuesday update trending toward full practice; Downs (calf) was back on the field Tuesday and called it very minor; Tuten's illness scare from last week was already a non-issue per Jacksonville beat writers — the real swing factor on his workload stays the 3-way RB rotation with Rodriguez and Allen. If Higgins, Flowers, or Downs is out: start Diggs. If Tuten is out: start Woody Marks.
Waivers / trades: TE depth is the priority add — you're rostering zero backup at the position, see the Waivers tab; there's also a real trade on the table for a bench TE, see Trades.

GAME OF THROWS (Yahoo) — correction: Isaiah Likely is healthy and a confirmed Week 1 starter, not a watch
Do now: nothing needs a change, but flagging a correction from the last update — Likely's "foot injury, unlikely to play" note was wrong. That was a stale 2025 article about his old team (the Ravens vs. Bills), not this year's Giants situation. He caught passes in Saturday's preseason finale, has no injury designation on your actual roster screenshot, and fantasy consensus has him locked in as the Giants' starting TE Sunday night. He starts.
Locks next 24h: none — first kickoff is Myers (SEA) Wednesday 5:20 PM PT
Lineup: Likely moves from watch to start — Dallas graded a bottom-5 defense in 2025 and he's the clear TE1 in a Sunday-nighter. Parker Washington's injury flag stays confirmed clean. Judkins still draws the toughest matchup on either roster (JAX run D, now an 8.5-pt road dog) but stays in — no better flex on the bench.
Waivers / trades: no visibility into other Yahoo rosters or free agents this run (private league, screenshots only cover your team and this week's opponent) — can't safely propose availability or a trade this week; see the Waivers tab for what to check yourself in the app.

FYI: Chase Brown starts in both leagues; Michael Wilson sits on both benches; four Jaguars are rostered across the two leagues (Tuten, Strange, Jaguars D/ST on Sleeper, Parker Washington on Yahoo). Checked the handcuffs behind your starting RBs — Perine (behind Chase Brown), Vidal/Mitchell (behind Hampton), Kendre Miller (behind Etienne) — nothing new; Perine's only recent injury note is a stale one from last November.

waivers.text:
SLEEPER — priority is TE depth: you're rostering zero backup at the position, and Strange shares Week 7's JAX/LAC bye cluster with Herbert, Hampton, Tuten, and your DEF, so it's worth building now while it's cheap. Your FAAB budget is untouched at $100 (nobody in the league has spent yet) and you sit waiver position 3.
1. Darren Waller (TE, CAR) — signed as Carolina's TE2 behind Tommy Tremble on paper, but far and away the more proven player with real path to overtaking the job. Drop Fernando Mendoza (your QB3, zero standalone value). FAAB $8.
2. Justice Hill (RB, BAL) — locked in as Derrick Henry's clear #2 and the passing-down back in a full-PPR league; has real standalone flex value on his own. Drop Zachariah Branch (WR, no role in ATL). FAAB $6.
3. AJ Barner (TE, SEA) — ascending sophomore, second TE flier if you miss on Waller or want a true handcuff pair. Drop Zavion Thomas (WR, no role in CHI). FAAB $4.
4. Cooper Kupp (WR, SEA) — surprisingly available; only worth a flier once you've addressed TE, as an upgrade over Branch/Thomas if he wins early targets. FAAB $5.
5. Roschon Johnson (RB, CHI) — cheap early-down insurance in a muddled Bears backfield; pure speculative stash. FAAB $3.
No DEF/K stream needed this week — Aubrey and the Jaguars D&ST both carry plus Week 1 matchups per the Analysis tab.

YAHOO — no access to the Yahoo free-agent pool this run (private league, no login, screenshots only). Likely being healthy actually lowers urgency at TE, but Okonkwo remains a thin TE2 if you want a stopgap plan. Drop a fresh screenshot of the free-agent list (Players > Available, filtered by position) into the War room Drive folder and next run can give you real availability and FAAB/bid guidance.

trades.text:
SLEEPER — send Stefon Diggs to Grandmasterfabe ("Master Bate$ LaPortapotty") for Jake Ferguson (TE, DAL). Diggs is stuck behind Higgins, Flowers, and Downs on your bench with no path to starting reps; Grandmasterfabe is stacked at WR (Olave, DeVonta Smith, Jameson Williams, Jakobi Meyers, Alec Pierce) but is rolling with rookie Harold Fannin as their only real TE, with Ferguson buried as insurance. Diggs gives them a proven bye-week/injury-fill starter; you turn a fully blocked bench piece into the backup TE you currently have nowhere on the roster, which matters with Strange sharing the Week 7 JAX/LAC bye cluster. It's a mild overpay in raw value on your side, justified by how scarce TE depth is around this league right now — nobody scanned so far is sitting on two startable options. Checked your Weeks 15-17 outlook first: Diggs isn't projected to be a playoff starter behind your current WR corps, so moving him costs you nothing down the stretch.

YAHOO — no trade idea this run. I don't have visibility into other managers' rosters or trade blocks in your private Yahoo league (screenshots only cover your team and this week's opponent), so I can't responsibly name a real deal. No trade.txt found in the War room folder either.

news.headline: Bengals' Tee Higgins: Dealing with heel injury
news.summary: Higgins is limited in practice this week with a heel contusion, but coach Zac Taylor says it isn't a major concern and expects him ready for kickoff.

news.headline: Ravens Got Good Zay Flowers News Ahead of Colts Week 1 Game
news.summary: Flowers received a positive Tuesday update on his quad injury and the Ravens expect him back to full practice and available for the opener.

news.headline: Jaguars' Bhayshul Tuten: Misses practice with illness
news.summary: Tuten was sent home from an early-week practice with an illness; beat writers already consider it a non-issue for Sunday.

news.headline: Josh Downs (calf) practices Tuesday
news.summary: Downs returned to practice Tuesday and continues to call his calf issue very minor and precautionary ahead of Week 1.

news.headline: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Week 1 Picks
news.summary: Likely is healthy and locked in as the Giants' starting tight end, with experts pegging him for TE1 upside against a bottom-5 Dallas defense in his Giants debut.

news.headline: Parker Washington (undisclosed) day-to-day
news.summary: The undisclosed issue that had Washington day-to-day in late August has resolved and he now carries no injury designation into Week 1.
